clue.text: Charged in advance to position on Don -faltered around the beginning of December

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the next piece, which sits inside them
to position things is to arrange them, so the letters of the following words are set in a new order
the beginning of a word is its opening letter, here taken from December

explanation.surface: A man called Don stumbles while getting into position as December arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to position' rearranges ON DON FALTERED, and 'around' wraps those letters round D, the first letter of December, giving the fourteen letters of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A front-loaded fee or charge is one taken at the outset of an investment, that is, paid up front.

clue.text: First class returns in stock issue: kind of loyalty, perhaps

indicators.note: the turned letters go in the middle of the word for stock

parts.note: to stock a shelf is to fill it

indicators.note: returns tells us that the first-class letters come back the other way

parts.note: A1 means first class, written here as the letters A and I

explanation.surface: A note about a share issue, with first-class returns, and some sort of loyalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' in the surface points at offspring, the very sense the definition carries: loyalty owed by a son or daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Filial describes what is due from a son or daughter to a parent, as in filial devotion or duty.

clue.text: A tenor performing baroque

indicators.note: performing suggests the letters are put through their paces and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A singer of the tenor part performs music of the Baroque period.
explanation.definitionFit: Baroque art and architecture is elaborately decorated, so baroque can mean highly ornamented.

clue.text: Two steaks, one with bone, seen on the card

parts.note: the T-bone is the steak with a bone, and its T is the letter taken
rump is a cut of steak

explanation.surface: A diner orders two steaks, one on the bone, from the menu card.
explanation.walkthrough: The two steaks are T-bone and rump; the first contributes only its T. A trump is a card from the suit that beats all others in a game such as bridge or whist.
explanation.definitionFit: A trump is a playing card of the suit ranking above the rest, printed on a card in the pack.

clue.text: Regular occurrence associated with gallantry, we hear

indicators.note: we hear marks a word that sounds like the required one when spoken

parts.note: chivalrous behaviour is associated with knights, so is described as knightly

explanation.surface: Something that happens regularly is linked, we are told, to gallant deeds.
explanation.walkthrough: The silent K means knightly and the answer sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that happens every night recurs regularly, at the same time each evening.

clue.text: See 1
Eton, for example, is very traditional

definitions.meaning: Eton College is an example of an alma mater, the institution one attended long ago
describing attitudes or methods that are conservative and old-fashioned

explanation.walkthrough: ETON is a famous English fee-paying boarding school near Windsor.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton is a long-established English public school, and the phrase also describes conservative, old-fashioned values.

clue.text: Soft return to make bogey

definitions.meaning: in tennis or squash, a gentle stroke that barely clears the net and dies
in golf, a bogey is one over par, i.e. losing one stroke

explanation.definitionFit: In racket sports it is a delicate stroke that falls just over the net; in golf, dropping a stroke means going one over par.

clue.text: Break off with girl on ship, meeting another just right

parts.note: Di is a short girl's name
SS stands for steamship
Eve is another girl's name
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A girl breaks off with her ship, meeting another woman who seems just right.
explanation.definitionFit: To dissever is to sever or split apart, an old-fashioned word for cutting off.

clue.text: Speaking style?

parts.note: reads as a manner of delivery, but the whole vocabulary and grammar of a tongue is a style in which people speak

explanation.definitionFit: A tongue such as French or Welsh is a system of words used for speaking; also the choice of words in speech.

clue.text: They are peripheral (commercial) university types

parts.note: a commercial is an advertisement, or ad
dons are university teachers, especially at Oxford and Cambridge

explanation.surface: Commercially minded academics are kept at the margins.
explanation.definitionFit: Extras such as accessories or optional features are attached to a main product, at its edges rather than its core.

clue.text: Growth in regency-style housing

indicators.note: housing means the words contain the answer inside them

explanation.surface: Something growing in a house built in the Regency style.
explanation.definitionFit: A cyst is a sac of fluid that grows abnormally in the body, a kind of growth.

clue.text: Opposition's against road to border of Mandalay

parts.note: anti means against
a path is a way or road

indicators.note: the border, here the far edge, of Mandalay is its last letter

explanation.surface: The opposition objects to a road to the border of the Burmese city of Mandalay.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipathy is strong dislike or hostility, a feeling of opposition towards something.

clue.text: Indian class throw out English

parts.note: to cast is to throw or fling

explanation.surface: An Indian school class expels an English pupil.
explanation.definitionFit: In traditional Hindu society people were born into a hereditary social rank of this kind.

clue.text: Affect the direction and method

parts.note: S, for south, is a compass direction
a way of doing something is a method

explanation.surface: A remark about influencing both where things go and how they are done.
explanation.definitionFit: To influence someone's opinion or decision is to have an effect on it.

clue.text: Engineer needs time to construct energy units

parts.note: James Watt was the Scottish engineer who improved the steam engine
hours are units of time

explanation.surface: An engineer needs time to build units of energy.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of electrical energy equal to one watt of power sustained for sixty minutes.

clue.text: Book Miss Piggy, perhaps, to return in duet

indicators.note: the reversed letters are placed inside the word for book

parts.note: a tome is a large book

indicators.note: to return here is to go back, so the word is read from its end

parts.note: Miss Piggy of the Muppets is a female pig, an example of a sow

explanation.surface: Booking the Muppet Miss Piggy to come back and sing a duet.
explanation.definitionFit: A duet is a performance by a pair, and a pair of people is a twosome.

clue.text: Cult perm, frizzy, as seen on the guitarist

indicators.note: frizzy hair is tightly curled and messed up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A frizzy perm of the sort fans copy from a cult rock guitarist.
explanation.definitionFit: A guitarist strums with a small pick held in the fingers, often worn on a necklace or seen in the hand.

clue.text: Dope follows joint in a kind of reflex action

indicators.note: follows puts the word for dope after the word for joint

parts.note: the knee is a joint of the leg
a dope is a fool, and so is a jerk

explanation.surface: A doped-up joint smoker reacts by reflex.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapping below the kneecap makes the leg kick automatically, the classic involuntary reflex; also an unthinking response.

clue.text: The French have one in their country: a jerk and a madman

parts.note: l' is French for the, before a vowel
un is French for one
a tic is a twitch or involuntary jerk

explanation.surface: The French have someone in their country: a twitching jerk and a madman.
explanation.definitionFit: A lunatic is an insane person, once thought to be affected by the moon.

clue.text: Newspaper writing about political leader is withdrawn

indicators.note: about means the word for withdrawn goes round the next piece

parts.note: coy means shy and reserved, so withdrawn

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, here of political

explanation.surface: A newspaper report about a political leader who has gone into hiding.
explanation.definitionFit: In journalism, copy is the text written for publication in a paper.

clue.text: African watercourse diverted via tree-line

indicators.note: diverted means sent back the other way, so the letters are read in reverse
via means by way of, so the answer is found travelling within the word that follows

explanation.surface: An African river is diverted along a line of trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'via' picks ELIN out of tree-line, and 'diverted' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: The world's longest river flows north through Africa into the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Vehicle found in terrible rain: it's paradise

indicators.note: found in means the vehicle is set inside the rearranged letters
terrible signals the letters are messed up into a new order

parts.note: a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A van caught in a terrible storm of rain: the driver calls it paradise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' turns RAIN into NIRA, and 'found in' puts VAN inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: In Buddhism, the state of perfect bliss and release, used loosely for heaven or bliss.

clue.text: Office furniture?

definitions.meaning: a government department or agency, such as an information desk
a writing desk with drawers, a piece of furniture

explanation.definitionFit: A government department is called this, and so is a writing desk with drawers, a piece of household furniture.

clue.text: Comment about something that's no longer legal tender

parts.note: re means about or concerning

parts.words: something that's no longer legal tender
parts.note: the mark was the German currency until the euro replaced it

explanation.surface: A remark on a banknote that can no longer be spent.
explanation.definitionFit: A remark is an observation or comment made in passing.

clue.text: In speech, look out for the national character

indicators.note: in speech means the word is heard spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: to check is to look out for or watch

explanation.surface: Keeping an ear out for the national accent when someone speaks.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of the Czech Republic is a national of that country, and a character is a person.

clue.text: EU respect is wavering for martyr

indicators.note: wavering suggests instability, so the letters shift into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Wavering European respect turns someone into a martyr.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to martyr someone is to torment or kill them for their beliefs.

clue.text: Play the divorce, at first being faithful

indicators.note: at first means the word for the divorcee comes before the word for play

parts.note: a divorced partner is an ex
an act is a part of a play, or to play is to act

explanation.surface: Acting out the divorce, being faithful at first.
explanation.definitionFit: An exact copy is faithful to its original, accurate in every detail.

clue.text: It may be negative, but did he arrive too late to save Troy?

definitions.meaning: a blood factor that is either positive or negative

definitions.text: did he arrive too late to save Troy?
definitions.meaning: the Thracian king who came to help Troy but was killed on the night he arrived

explanation.definitionFit: The blood-group factor named after a monkey, and the Thracian king in Homer slain by Odysseus and Diomedes before he could fight.

clue.text: Chinese people take in sailor, with time to dance

indicators.note: take in means the people hold the sailor inside them

parts.note: the Han are the majority ethnic group of China
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Chinese people take in a sailor and make time to dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A habanera is a slow Cuban dance in duple time, made famous by the aria in Carmen.

clue.text: Trains a youngster to race and quickly profits

definitions.meaning: taken literally, getting a young deer to run fast
earns money rapidly, often by dubious means

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means earning easy money fast; read literally it describes speeding up a young male deer.
